title: Anterior Segment Organ Culture Platform for Tracking Open Globe Injuries and Therapeutic Performance
protocol: Prepare and gas-sterilize ASOC dishes for each eye.
Gas-sterilize clamping rings for each eye.
Sterilize fluidic connectors with O-rings for each eye.
Sterilize two 18 G needle hubs for each eye.
Sterilize four screws for each eye.
Prepare two lengths of PE-100 tubing long enough to extend from the dish inside the incubator to the syringe pump and pressure transducer data collection setup for each eye.
Sterilize two 18 G 90° bent needle hubs for each eye.
Sterilize two 3-way valves for each eye.
Prepare and autoclave the micro-dissection instrument kit.
Prepare and autoclave the assembly instrument kit.
Autoclave a daily kit containing one L-key per day of culture.
Autoclave four 100 mL beakers for disinfecting and storing eyes and anterior segments.
Autoclave the puncture objects.
Gather Petri dishes, gauze, dish stand, syringes, and nylon syringe filters.
Prepare sterile media: DMEM with 4% FBS, 1x Glutamax, 1x Gentamicin, 1x Antibiotic-Antimycotic (AA).
Prepare AA-PBS: PBS with 1x Antibiotic-Antimycotic.
Clean and dry large surgical scissors and forceps for gross dissection.
Gather supplies from gross dissection tool pack.
Place enucleated porcine eyes submerged in PBS and on ice.
Lay out the surgical drape.
Transfer items required for gross dissection onto the laid-out surgical drape.
Gather supplies from micro-dissection instrument kit.
Prepare sterile gauze, dissecting microscope, betadine solution, sterile PBS, sterile media, four sterilized 100 mL beakers, and sterile Petri dish.
Aseptically transfer to BSC II cabinet #1.
Set up the cabinet for visualizing eyes on the dissecting microscope.
Gather gas-sterilized kits (dish kit and lid kit), assembly instrument kit, sterile media, dish stands, sterile Petri dishes, sterile syringes, and syringe filters.
Aseptically transfer to BSC II cabinet #2.
Set up the cabinet for dish assembly.
Transfer stabilized eyes ready for puncture to a BSC II cabinet when they are 72 h post-setup.
Prepare pneumatic powered injury induction device (assembly detailed in Supplemental 3).
Set up Lab Jack and cross-tracking vise to hold the ASOC dish.
Cut away the extraorbital tissue and trim the conjunctiva leaving only the corneoscleral shell and optic nerve.
Perform the dissection under non-sterile conditions with large surgical scissors and forceps.
Place the eyes back into fresh PBS on ice until all eyes required for experimental setup have been preliminary/gross dissected.
Submerge the eyes in 10% betadine solution for 2 min in closed containers.
Transfer the eyes aseptically to BSC II cabinet #1.
Perform all subsequent works under sterile conditions to minimize contaminations during setup.
Sterilely dissect anterior segments.
Transfer the eyes into three serial washes of sterile AA-PBS to remove excess betadine solution from the ocular surface while maintaining sterility of the ocular tissue.
Maintain the tissue in AA-PBS until further use.
Hemisect the eye using a razor blade or scalpel and curved scissors.
Place the eye on an AA-PBS-soaked gauze.
Create an incision with a sterile razor blade or scalpel near the equator of the eye (60/40 split with 40 on the anterior side).
Using curved surgical scissors, hemisect the eye to isolate the anterior eye (corneal half).
Use microscissors to scoop vitreous humor from the anterior segment.
Remove the lens from the anterior segment using microscissors.
Place the anterior segments in AA-PBS until further dissection steps.
Cut back iris to iris root gradually and radially with a dissecting microscope until trabecular meshwork (TM) is visible.
Cut 360° around the iris at the same depth as the initial cut into the tissue to expose the entire TM region.
Clean up any remaining residual iris covering TM as necessary.
Trim the ciliary body remnants posterior to the TM, leaving only a thin band of tissue posterior to the TM region (approximately 1 mm).
Place the dissected anterior segment in media until further setup in ASOC.
Place a single anterior segment (AS) in a Petri dish with the cup facing up.
Wet a cotton swab in the media and gently dab it in the center of the cornea to remove pigment.
Hold the eye with forceps and wipe around the sclera with the same swab to remove extra pigment.
Invert the AS and place it on top of the bottom part of the dish over the elevated region, centering the cornea over the elevated area.
Place a clamping ring on top of the newly placed AS.
Insert four screws into corresponding holes to hold the ring in place with the AS underneath.
Gently hand-tighten the screws using an L-key.
Cover the Petri dish setup with its lid and invert it.
Attach the dish stand.
Attach fluidic connectors with O-rings to threaded ports on the bottom of the dish.
To one fluidic connector, attach a 18 G 90° bent needle hub, tubing, another 18 G needle hub, a nylon syringe filter, a three-way valve, and a 20 mL syringe filled with media.
Attach an 18 G 90° bent needle hub to the second fluidic connector.
Connect tubing, another 18 G needle hub, and a three-way valve to the second connector.
Attach the barrel portion of a sterile 10 mL syringe to the second connector as a reservoir.
Gently push media through the system using the fluidics connector port identified in step 3.5 to inflate the AS, fill media in the tubing, and eventually the reservoir.
Remove bubbles by gently pushing media into the dish and inverting the dish to push out the bubbles and into the reservoir.
Place the dish and stand upright.
Attach a Petri dish bottom portion underneath the feet of the stand carefully not to ensnarl the tubing.
Direct tubing lines out through the bottom of the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator door so that they do not interfere with the opening and closing of the door.
Place the ASOC dish into the cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for incubation.
Attach a 20 mL syringe to the syringe pump set at 2.5 µL/min.
Position the tubing line with the reservoir at the pressure transducer instrument.
Connect the side 3-way valve to the pressure transducer setup.
Flow PBS through the line to avoid air bubbles entering the tubing lines.
Empty the PBS from the reservoirs after setting up to reduce contamination risk.
Ensure a microSD card is present for data file saving.
Turn on the pressure transducer setup to begin IOP data collection.
Remove the dishes from the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator and place them into the BSC II cabinet after 24 h of equilibration.
Check for leaks under each dish on the Petri plate.
Check for tight fluidic connections under the dish if leaks are present.
Tighten the screws in the clamping ring using a sterile L-key to check for leaks at the dish top.
Aspirate the media from the dish well.
Prepare the BSC II cabinet for OG injury induction as detailed in step 1.10.
Connect the puncture platform to a compressed air line.
Attach the sterile puncture object to the chuck.
Set the pressure regulator on the puncture platform to 50 psi.
Position the cross-tracking vise in front of the puncture platform.
Remove the ASOC dish from the incubator and place it in the cross-tracking vise perpendicular to the puncture platform.
Extend the piston arm to its maximal distance.
Position the corneal apex within 1 mm of the puncture object.
Retract the piston arm, bringing the anterior segment 1 cm closer to the puncture object.
Fire the puncture device by turning it on and opening the solenoid valve with the second switch.
Verify proper injury induction by visual inspection.
Remove ASOC dish from the vise and place the lid back onto the dish assembly.
Open the fluidic line to the pressure transducer.
Place the ASOC back into the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Remove ASOC dishes from the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Close the 3-way valve to the syringe and reservoir.
Disconnect the tubing from the system.
Discard the syringe, reservoir, and filter.
Place the 3-way valves, tubing, and needle hubs in a container for washing and sterilizing.
Disconnect the needle hubs from the fluidic connections on the bottom of the dish.
Unthread the fluidic connectors and o-rings.
Remove the four screws from the clamping ring using the L-key.
Carefully remove the clamping ring.
Using forceps, remove the AS from the dish.
Place the AS in fixative or appropriate biohazard waste depending on endpoint analysis and image requirements.
Connect the microSD card to a computer to remove the .txt file containing data from the most recent experimental run.
Import the data into a spreadsheet.
Organize the data into 12 columns: Time (in min) and mV signal for each of 11 pressure transducer channels.
Plot control channel versus time to confirm mV signal was consistent throughout.
Convert the mV signals for ten channels into mmHg using slope-intercept equations generated from the initial calibration of each sensor.
Plot time (convert to days to simplify data interpretation) versus each of the ten channels to determine how the IOP fluctuated across the experimental time course.
Determine average IOP values at key points in the data to more easily compare values between each and how they are altered before and after OG injury induction.
Average 2-3 h of data for each 24 h interval to determine IOP at each day of ASOC.
